Be concise; excerpts not whole files. Also describe the overlay's visual (icon, position on shape, count badge) so we can mirror the design.

- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. * `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

content.text:
**The overlay you're porting no longer exists on Roam's canvas.** It was removed in #1288 (ENG-2096). On canvas, Roam now shows discourse context in a "Context" tab of the tldraw style panel when a discourse node is selected (#1272, ENG-2037). And there is no separate canvas overlay toggle in current Roam.

That leaves two possible parity targets: the old removed overlay, or the current Context tab. Both are described below.

Paths below are relative to `/Users/trang.doan/Desktop/code/discourse-graph/.claude/worktrees/eng-2279-add-discourse-context-overlay-to-obsidian-canvas/apps/roam/`.

## 1. How the overlay appeared on the canvas

**Before #1288 (the removed overlay).** Source is `git show b80fe05eb^:apps/roam/src/components/canvas/DiscourseNodeUtil.tsx`; line numbers are approximate, taken from the diff hunks.
- **Where:** it rendered inside `DiscourseNodeUtil.component()` (~L770), at the top-right of the shape (`absolute right-1 top-1`). Its container stopped pointer-down so tldraw didn't start a drag. It passed `opacity="50"` and used the shape's text colour for text and icon.
- **Trigger:** it mounted lazily on the first `onPointerEnter` on the shape (~L633, sets `overlayMounted`). Once mounted, the badge stayed visible.
- **Gating:** it only rendered when the "Overlay in canvas" setting was on (read once, ~L472). #1287 (ENG-2060) then hid it for `blck-node` and `page-node` shapes.
- **Badge:** `DiscourseContextButton` in `src/components/DiscourseContextOverlay.tsx:105-164`.
  - It's a small, minimal Blueprint `Button` showing `[diagram-tree icon] {score}  [link icon] {refs}`.
  - Icons are 10px (`ICON_SIZE`, L103), text is `text-xs`, and it pulses while loading with counts shown as "-".
  - `score` is the node type's "Overlay" attribute; by default that's the relation count (L191-201).
  - `refs` is the number of blocks referencing the page (datalog query, L49-51).
- **Click:** opens a Blueprint `Popover` below the badge (L243-287). It holds `ContextContent` (`src/components/DiscourseContext.tsx:106`), the same UI as the page's discourse context:
  - one tab per relation label, titled `(${count}) ${label}` (L206);
  - a "Group By Target" checkbox (L226);
  - results rendered as Roam links.
- **No canvas actions:** the popover had no add-to-canvas and no drag onto the canvas.

**Now (#1272, the Context tab).** This lives in `src/components/canvas/CustomStylePanel.tsx`.
- **Trigger:** selecting exactly one discourse node (not `blck-node` or `page-node`) shows the style panel with two tabs, "Context" (default) and "Styling" (L377-407, L409-440).
- **`ContextTabContent` (L45):**
  - Shows "Loading relations...", "Failed to load relations." or "No relations found."
  - Results are grouped by relation label, with a small grey `text-xs font-semibold` heading per group.
  - Each row shows the truncated node text as a Roam block string.
  - Each row has a +/− minimal button, "Add node to canvas" / "Remove node from canvas" (L320-370).
- **Toggle (`toggleNodeOnCanvas`, L270):**
  - If the related node is already on the canvas, it deletes it.
  - Otherwise it creates the shape in a column 240px away (`NEW_NODE_OFFSET_PX`, L41), finding a free spot in that column.
  - It then draws the relation arrow (L158-180) and brings the new node into view.
  - If "Auto canvas relations" is on, it also creates the node's other existing relations (L259-264).
  - A pending set guards against creating duplicates.
  - Failures show the toast "Failed to update the canvas for this result."

## 2. Settings

**Removed canvas toggle.** Roam used to have a separate canvas toggle; #1288 deleted it.
- Title "(BETA) Overlay in canvas"; description "Whether or not to overlay discourse context information over canvas nodes." with a docs link.
- Stored as personal key `"Overlay in canvas"`, default `false`, in the zod schema and in block props.
- Legacy extension-settings key `discourse-context-overlay-in-canvas` (was in `src/data/userSettings.ts`).
- Rendered with `PersonalFlagPanel` in `HomePersonalSettings.tsx`.

**Page/markdown overlay (still present).**
- Title "Overlay"; description "Whether or not to overlay discourse context information over discourse node references." plus a link to `ROAM_DOCS.discourseContextOverlay`.
- Key `PERSONAL_KEYS.discourseContextOverlay = "Discourse context overlay"` (`src/components/settings/utils/settingKeys.ts:22`), default `false` (`zodSchema.ts:250`), legacy key `discourse-context-overlay` (`accessors.ts:223`).
- Rendered in `src/components/settings/HomePersonalSettings.tsx:152-166`.
- Also has a command-palette toggle (`src/utils/registerCommandPaletteCommands.ts:415`) and is applied at load (`src/utils/initializeObserversAndListeners.ts:248`).
- Per node type, an "Overlay" setting picks which attribute feeds the badge's score (`NodeConfig.tsx:452-466`, `DISCOURSE_NODE_KEYS.overlay`).

**Current HEAD layout.** In `Settings.tsx:198-277`, "Personal Settings" has Home / Queries / Canvas / Left sidebar. The Canvas tab (L223-232) only holds `CanvasShortcutSettings` (per-node-type shortcut checkbox + key input, "Default: X"). "Auto canvas relations" still sits in Home (`HomePersonalSettings.tsx:228-240`).

**The reorg (#1373, ENG-2189, commit 7847403f6).** It is only on `origin/roam-setting-overhaul` and related eng-218x branches; it is not in this worktree's HEAD. It replaces the Personal/Global split with topic sections:
- **Preferences:** General, Styling
- **Features:** Discourse context, Canvas, Left sidebar
- **Grammar:** Nodes, Relations
- **Node types:** one tab per node type
- **Advanced:** Queries, Export
- **Admin**

Tab ids are in `settings/utils/settingsTabs.ts`, e.g. `features-discourse-context`, `features-canvas`. Old ids are aliased, e.g. `canvas-shortcuts-personal-settings` maps to `features-canvas`.

The Features > Canvas tab (`CanvasSettings.tsx`) contains, in order:
1. "Canvas Page Format", global text: "The page format for canvas pages"
2. "Discourse tool keyboard shortcut", personal: "Set a single key to activate the discourse tool in tldraw. Only single keys (no modifiers) are supported. Leave empty for no shortcut." Placeholder "Click to set single key".
3. "Auto canvas relations", personal flag: "Automatically add discourse relations to canvas when a node is added"
4. Section heading "Node on canvas", followed by the per-node-type shortcuts.

Features > Discourse context (`DiscourseContextSettings.tsx`) holds only the "Overlay" toggle above. There is no canvas-specific overlay toggle there either. If Obsidian adds one, the closest Roam precedent is the removed "(BETA) Overlay in canvas", default off.

## 3. Performance
- **Old canvas overlay:** mounted only after the first pointer-enter, and the setting was read once per render via `useMemo`.
- **Page overlay:** `Wrapper` uses `useInViewport` and shows a disabled "-/-" placeholder until the reference is on screen (`DiscourseContextOverlay.tsx:331-362`). Counts are fetched on mount, not on click.
- **Caching:** `getDiscourseContextResults` has a cache; it's bypassed with `ignoreCache` on refresh. `useDiscourseContextMutationRefresh` refetches when relations change, which keeps a closed popover's counts from going stale (L236-238).
- **Context tab:** loads only when a single node is selected, cancels in-flight results when the selection changes, and bypasses the cache only after a mutation (`refreshCount > 0`, `CustomStylePanel.tsx:58-81`).

## 4. Relevant commits
- `b80fe05eb` [ENG-2096] Remove the discourse context overlay from Roam canvas (#1288)
- `be9349580` ENG-2037 Add tabbed node card context menu to Roam tldraw (#1272)
- `da2861f32` ENG-2060 Remove discourse context overlay button from blocks on canvas (#1287)
- `378372df3` ENG-1140 Implement simplified discourse context overlay (#1294)
- `7847403f6` ENG-2189 Reorganize Roam settings into four topic-based sections (#1373) — not in HEAD
- `5ddf58636` ENG-739 Move color selector from Canvas to General tab (#945)
- `69593ede9` ENG-1660 Dual-write canvas node shortcuts (#1046)
- `4ba4c7362` [ENG-2088] Add tag to block button on canvas block cards (#1351)

The Obsidian page-overlay work is also on this branch: `c71d3237e` #1433, `608c6b079` #1434, `c8e0f6ffc` #1435.

**Decision for you:** mirror the old badge-plus-popover overlay, which Roam dropped, or the current Context tab with add/remove-to-canvas buttons. Either way, the reorg puts overlay settings under "Discourse context" and canvas settings under "Canvas", and neither tab has a canvas overlay toggle.
